title: Honeydew Melon Sorbet
changes_from_base: Ripe honeydew with a light sugar and corn syrup and lime replaces the mango.
summary: A pale green, gently sweet sorbet of ripe honeydew melon brightened with lime.

ingredients.item: light corn syrup or glucose syrup
ripe honeydew or other green-fleshed melon (about 1600 g)
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Syrup
steps.text: Heat the water and sugar in the small pan until it boils and turns clear, then stir in the corn syrup and cool.

steps.title: Prepare the melon
steps.text: Halve it, scoop out the seeds, cut away the rind and dice the flesh; you need about 900 g.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Whizz the melon with the cool syrup, lime juice and salt until smooth. A very ripe melon needs no more sugar than this.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Refrigerate for at least 2 h or overnight, and put the empty container in the freezer.

steps.title: Churn
steps.text: Blend again for a few seconds, then churn for 20-25 min.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Pack into the cold container and freeze for 2 h; it sets firm, so soften in the fridge for 15-20 min before scooping.

tips: A ripe honeydew smells sweet at the stem end and gives slightly when pressed.
Cantaloupe or Galia melon work the same way.
Add a few mint leaves to the blender for a fresher taste.
storage: Keep covered in the freezer for up to 1 week; sorbet turns icy after that. Soften for 10 min before scooping.
